comparisons.peer_topic: Consumer Lending net income and revenue drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Net income for Consumer Lending increased $334 million to $3.2 billion, driven primarily by higher revenue including a $717 million increase in net interest income and an $85 million increase in noninterest income.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Bank of America reported significant growth in Net Interest Income (NII) for 2024, but they attributed this growth to different primary drivers. JPM's NII rose 24% primarily due to balance sheet actions, specifically reinvestments in the investment securities portfolio. In contrast, Bank of America's Consumer Lending segment saw NII increase by $717 million (to $11.9 billion), driven primarily by the impact of higher loan balances rather than reinvestment strategies.

comparisons.peer_summary: Net interest income for 2024 was $8.06 billion, representing a 27% increase from 2023, driven by higher interest income from trading assets, investments, and collateralized agreements due to higher balances and rates, partially offset by a decrease in deposits with banks.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs reported substantial percentage increases in Net Interest Income for 2024, driven by a combination of rate impacts and balance sheet dynamics. JPMorgan's NII increased 24% driven by balance sheet actions (reinvestments in securities) partially offset by rates. Goldman Sachs' NII increased 27%, driven by higher interest income from trading assets and investments reflecting higher average balances and higher average interest rates, partially offset by lower deposit income.

sentences.text: Net interest income was $9.8 billion, up 24%, driven by the impact of balance sheet actions, primarily reinvestments in the investment securities portfolio, partially offset by the net impact of rates.

Net interest income in the consolidated statements of earnings was $8.06 billion for 2024, 27% higher than 2023, reflecting an increase in interest income, partially offset by an increase in interest expense.

The increase in interest income primarily related to trading assets and investments (each reflecting the impact of higher average balances and higher average interest rates), collateralized agreements and other interest-earning assets (each reflecting the impact of higher average interest rates), partially offset by a decrease in interest income related to deposits with banks (reflecting the impact of lower average balances).
